Running a newsletter business (MailCheap — $3,500 MRR) is so different from running a web analytics business (DataFast — $28,000 MRR).

Web analytics are perceived as “nice.” I beg my users to spend enough time to get to the “aha” moment and stick with my product. Adoption takes time. Conversion rate is low.

On the other hand, a newsletter is someone’s business backbone. If the user can’t send emails, they don’t make money. I reject ~50% of senders to protect deliverability on MailCheap, and every day I get users on support begging me to reinstate their accounts. Conversion rate is much higher.

It took DataFast 10 months to get where MailCheap got in 1.5 months.

🇺🇸 Investors are throwing billions at chip stocks despite the recent sell-off.

On November 23 alone, a reported $1.71 billion flowed into SOXL, a fund designed to deliver 3x the daily returns of a semiconductor index.

Another $1.62 billion went into SOXX, a regular semiconductor ETF, making the two funds the second and third largest recipients of U.S. ETF inflows that day.

But just a day later, SOXL lost nearly 25% of its net asset value.

That's the catch with leverage. It can turn a good day into a great one, but it can make a bad day a whole lot worse.

SOXL investors are betting on a recovery and using leverage to make the most of it.

Source: ETF. com, Direxion / Writer: Daniyal
